description: What holds a quit of the application, or an `octoboardd stop`, up: the daemon's stop check (coordinator/stop_check.rs, holds_quit and terminal_holds_quit) and a window's quit confirmation (packages/ui/src/lifecycle/useAppExit.ts, quitHolders) both read the sessions with the status a client is shown. A Rust test and a UI test both run every case, so that the two copies of the rule stay in step. `background` is whether the session has work left running in the background.

cases.name: starting, working and dormant sessions hold it up
a session waiting for the user holds it up
an idle session holds it up only with work left in the background
an interrupted or archived session does not hold it up
only a running shell terminal that is busy holds it up
